(a) RUN exits = the §2.9 stop-kind taxonomy, one row per core/stops.ts STOP_KINDS entry, with the §2.9 normative fact that EVERY kind writes report.md. (b) PROCESS exits = one row per operator-runnable entry point (bash scripts/test-conductor.sh, node conductor/tools/replay.ts, scripts/serve.py, llama-router), 0 = success plus the stated non-zero meaning. (c) ERROR envelopes = the three shapes an operator will actually see in a log: the router's 503 admission envelope (admission.hpp:52-58), the gated-tool deny (a thrown Error whose message IS the gate reason, relayed to the model — tools.ts:219-223 + plugin/index.ts:11-13, including the fail-closed gate-crash prefix), and the fan-out `{kind:'env', reason, errors}` completion (fanout.ts:308-321). REASONING: an ops doc's exit tables exist so an operator can tell 'the run ended' from 'the process died'; a stop kind is the run's exit code and the four commands are the process ones. Anything narrower (e.g. only evidence-record exitCode fields) would not be operable.

the 'publish denied stale' troubleshooting entry states the §2.6 freshness rule as its two conditions (the verify's startedMs must be at or after the newest staged-file mtime, and the verify record's head must equal current HEAD, the second skipped only in no-git mode), names the two ordinary causes — an edit landed after the verify started, or HEAD moved under it via a branch switch or a sibling item's publish — and gives the operator action: re-run validate to produce a fresh verify, then publish. It records the two behaviours 9.5b pins so the operator is not surprised: publish auto-re-verifies EXACTLY ONCE on a stale verdict, and a failing auto re-verify drops the item back to GREEN with debugging set rather than looping

the 'run disengaged' troubleshooting entry states the §3.7 rule that three consecutive futile idle re-prompts — futile meaning the run-state signature did not change — produce stop kind `noop` plus a `disengage` anomaly in anomalies.jsonl, tells the operator to read the futile re-prompt entries in the journal, and names exactly the three continuation events that carry them (component `continuation`: reprompt, idle, disengage — the full EVENTS['continuation'] list at journal-events.ts:50). It states that the run still writes a stop-report and that the disengage backstop is a bound on the failure mode, not a fix (§9 limit 2)

OPERATIONS.md documents the two degraded modes an operator will actually meet. §3.9 no-git: conductor_setup offers exactly one choice when the workspace is not a repo — initialize a repo, or run in no-git mode, which sets git.mode 'read-only', DISABLES publish (items terminate at REVIEWED with their diff recorded in the report), disables worktree mode, drops the HEAD term from the freshness rule, and skips .git/info/exclude registration, leaving FSM, gates, evidence and review unchanged. Second session: .conductor/state/run.lock is an ADVISORY single-writer lock, the second conductor session gets read-only conductor, a dead holder's lock is broken automatically (24h default staleness, state.ts:38), a read-only instance never deletes the lock it observed, and a human deleting the lock lies to both sessions
